subject: telescope
pitch: A brass explorer's telescope on a wooden tripod. A long tube in polished brass with leather-wrapped sections and engraved rings, a smaller finder scope on top, an eyepiece with a rubber cup, focusing knobs, and a mahogany tripod with brass fittings and a little tray holding a rolled star chart.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for the tripod structure, using simple builder helpers to keep the API usage safe, and sketching out basic dimensions like a tripod height around 1.4m with the tube pivot near 1.25m and tube length of 1.0m.

Now I'm working out the tube's tilt angle (~20°) and orientation, with the objective end pointing forward and up while the eyepiece sits lower toward the rear. I'm setting up a root joint and a tripod head joint, then computing an axis direction and center point so I can place tube segments, leather wraps, and decorative rings along that axis using rods, lathes, and oriented torus shapes with appropriate colors for brass and leather details.

Adding the objective hood, lens glass disc, rear tube section, eyepiece, and rubber cup using tapered rods and lathes, then computing a perpendicular "up" vector to position a small finder scope with brackets, posts, and a front bell above the main tube.

Now I'm placing focus knobs on both sides of the tube as knurled cylinders along the x-axis with brass accents, then building the yoke mount—a head block with pivot axis and cradle arms (rods with pivot bolts) supporting the tube from below.

Next I'm designing the mahogany tripod: three tapered legs radiating from the head at equal angular spacing down to feet positioned on a circle, with brass collar bands near the top, a mid-leg brass ring, and brass caps at the flat-ended feet.

I'll add a thin brass rim around the tray edges, then place a rolled star chart as a cream cylinder with a darker spiral pattern on the ends, tied with two red ribbon torus rings, computing the triangle's radius at tray height (k≈0.565, giving roughly 0.35) to center it on the tray centroid.

For the legs I'm considering a wood grain paint along the y-axis even though they're tilted, and deciding whether to keep the brass tube flat-colored or add subtle countershading.

Setting up the joint hierarchy now - a root base joint, a head joint above it, and a tube joint aimed along a direction vector, with helper functions to compute points along the rod and torus geometry for the structure.

I'm planning the main brass rod spanning the shaft length, leather wrap sections at specific intervals, and thin raised rod rings alternating with torus beads as decorative bands along the shaft.

Then I'm building out the objective end: brass rod sections forming the bell and dew shield with a glass lens circle capping it, followed by a drawtube and collar at the rear for the eyepiece assembly.

Continuing the rear eyepiece: a rubber eyecup rod tapering to a dark blue-ish eyelens circle facing away from the objective, checking it clears the floor, then adding focus knob shafts and cylinders on each side at u=-0.28.

Now I'm placing the yoke arms connecting to the pivot, with a brass pivot bolt and a cross-plate box forming the head...

Adding tripod post, hexagonal wood head block, and brass hinge spheres at leg tops...

Leg radius tapers from 0.032 to 0.02 along its length. For the finder scope, I'm placing a brass body rod, a bell-shaped front with a lens circle, a rear tube, and a black eyepiece cup, plus mounting posts, a torus ring bracket, and a foot block connecting it to the main tube.

I'll skip extra details like a label plate, decal text, or compass, and just add small sphere screws for adjustment knobs. I'm setting up the color palette—brass, leather, mahogany, rubber, glass, paper, ribbon—and applying a wood grain texture to the mahogany parts.

For the chart roll, I'm positioning a cylinder along the x-axis with red ring markers near its ends, and working out the tray's triangular geometry so the chart sits correctly within its half-width at z=-0.03.

For the legs, I'm placing three at 0°, 120°, and 240° angles with one pointing forward, using a foot radius of 0.6.
